Monthly summary

    Your monthly summary will appear here after your first weigh-in.

    Each month starts with the 14-day average as it began and ends with the average on its last day, so it picks up where the month before ended. When the log starts partway through a month, or has a break of more than two weeks, a date shows which day an average comes from. The weekly trend is as it stood on the month’s last day, and milestones show in the month your average first reached them.

    Body fat

    DateWaist14-day average14-day avg.Body fatEdit measurement

    An estimate from the U.S. Army’s one-site tape formula, using your waist at the navel and your 14-day average on the day you measured. A tape estimate can be several points off a lab scan, so it’s most useful for following your own trend.

    What Baseline keeps about you, where it’s kept and who handles it, and how to download or delete it. The health data privacy policy has the details.

    What Baseline stores

    Your log
    Weigh-ins and their notes, waist measurements and the body fat formula you chose, your height and goal, your units and what the overview shows, and your reminder time and time zone. In Baseline’s database at Neon, in the United States, until you delete it.
    Reminder devices
    A push address for each device you turn reminders on from, in the same database, until you turn reminders off.
    Your agreement
    Which version of the health data policy you agreed to, and when, in the same database.
    Your account
    Your email address, your name and picture if you sign in with Google, and a record of your sign-ins, such as the browser and IP address. Kept by Clerk, which runs sign-in. None of your log goes to Clerk.
    On this device
    A copy of your log and any changes waiting to sync, so Baseline opens offline. Signing out removes them.

    What Baseline never does

    • No analytics, ads or trackers. The only code on Baseline’s pages that isn’t its own is Clerk’s sign-in, which can add a bot check from Cloudflare when you sign up.
    • No location. The time zone saved with a reminder is the only clue to where you are.
    • Your data is never sold or used for ads, and goes to no one but the services below.

    Who handles it

    Vercel
    Runs Baseline’s site and server. Its logs record each request’s IP address, and the server’s errors, which can include a value that failed to save. They’re kept for up to a day.
    Neon
    Hosts the database, in the United States. Deleted data stays in its restore history for up to 6 hours.
    Clerk
    Runs sign-in and keeps your account.
    Push services
    Apple, Google, Microsoft or Mozilla, depending on your browser, deliver reminders if you turn them on. Each reminder is encrypted, so they can’t read it.

    Your agreement

    To the health data privacy policy of . Withdrawing your agreement deletes your log, as Delete my data does, and Baseline asks again before it saves anything new.

    Download or delete

    Download

    Your weigh-ins as a spreadsheet, with each one’s note and 14-day average. Or everything in your log as JSON: weigh-ins and notes, waist measurements, height, the body fat formula, your goal, units, what the overview shows, reminder time and your agreement to the health data policy.

    Delete

    Delete my data empties your log on every device and keeps your account.

    Delete your data?

    This permanently deletes everything in your log, on every device:

    • Your weigh-ins and their notes
    • Your waist measurements and the body fat formula you chose
    • Your goal and your height
    • Your settings, which go back to kg and cm, with BMI and body fat shown
    • Your reminders, which stop on every device
    • Your agreement to the health data policy, so Baseline asks again before it saves anything new
